answer: A desert oasis guards one spring of nectar behind a narrow gate. Each identity must carry one jar from it, and the jars follow the Lucas count: the first holds 1 measure, the second 3, then 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, 47, 76, and the tenth 123. One keeper fills one jar at a time, so no farmer of fakes can split the work: twenty fakes demand 39,600 measures in all. A whisper of a shortcut dies at the gate: no jar can be bought ready-made; each must be drawn, carried, and sealed in turn. Like a password that gains a letter with every guess, the price of the next fake always outruns the last.
